title: LLM generation latency breached its anomaly band
summary: LLM call p95 rose from a flat 0.2375s baseline to 9.75s during the ten minute failure window (14:15:06Z-14:25:06Z) and returned to 0.2375s by 14:31:00Z. Calls kept completing throughout, so this was a slowdown in the generation path rather than an outage.
hypotheses: The generation step itself slowed down. insighthub:llm_latency_p95:5m went from 0.2375 at 14:10:00Z to 9.75 at 14:20:30Z while insighthub_llm_call_latency_seconds_count kept climbing (0 at 14:15:30Z, 19 at 14:20:30Z, 36 at 14:25:00Z), so calls were completing, just slowly. A failing provider would have stopped the count or raised the error ratio instead.

The delay sits inside generation, not retrieval. insighthub:rag_latency_p95:5m rose from 0.095 to exactly 9.75 at the same timestamp as the LLM p95; RAG latency wraps the LLM call, so the added time is accounted for entirely by the generation step.

The anomaly band behaved correctly. insighthub:llm_latency_p95:anomaly_upper read 0.2375 while the incident was live at 14:20:30Z and only widened to 8.3833 at 14:31:00Z, after recovery. The ten minute baseline offset kept the band from absorbing the failure it was measuring.

Recovery matches the injection boundary: p95 was back at 0.2375 at 14:31:00Z, six minutes after the injected delay was removed at 14:25:06Z, which is the time a 5 minute quantile window needs to roll past the slow calls.
root_cause: A deliberate 6000ms delay was injected into the fixture generation path via CHAOS_LLM_EXTRA_LATENCY_MS, applied by scripts/chaos/inject-llm-latency.sh. The metric window matches the injection window, and the configured delay accounts for the observed shift in p95.
correlation: LLM p95 and RAG p95 reached the same 9.75s at the same timestamp, isolating the change to the generation step.
The call counter kept increasing through the window, which separates a slow dependency from a failing or absent one.
The band stayed at its pre-incident value during the failure and widened only afterwards, as designed.
remediation: Remove the injected delay by clearing CHAOS_ENABLED and CHAOS_LLM_EXTRA_LATENCY_MS on the api deployment.
For a real provider slowdown, PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS bounds how long a single call may block before it becomes an error instead of latency.
Consider a separate alert on generation latency versus retrieval latency so the two can be distinguished without reading both panels.

detection.condition: p95 above mean+3*stddev of the offset one hour baseline, and above a 0.5s floor, sustained for 2m

evidence_source.note: Every value below was read from Prometheus, not authored by a model.
